subject: Future Tech
title: Shor's Factoring Threat
description: A micro-lesson that makes Shor's Factoring Threat usable.

hook.text: In 1994, Peter Shor showed a quantum computer could factor huge numbers exponentially faster than classical ones.

buildup.text: Modern encryption relies on the fact that factoring large numbers takes classical computers an impractical time.

discovery.text: Shor's algorithm uses quantum Fourier transforms to find hidden periods, which reveal the prime factors.

twist.text: If a large quantum machine runs Shor's algorithm, RSA encryption protecting banks and governments shatters.

climax.text: No one has factored a meaningful number yet. The machines are too noisy, but the threat reshapes cryptography.

punchline.text: One algorithm threatened the world's digital locks.

quiz.question: What does Shor's algorithm primarily threaten?
